water.adequate: Irrigation should be applied only as needed to maintain soil moisture near field capacity and to avoid unnecessary water application.
water.dry: Immediate irrigation is critically required to restore soil moisture above the permanent wilting threshold. Larger irrigation volumes should be applied promptly to re-establish soil moisture toward field capacity and to prevent irreversible crop stress and yield loss.
water.mid: More frequent irrigation with appropriate water volumes is recommended to restore soil moisture toward field capacity.

nutrient.deficit: Increase fertilizer application rate to restore nutrient balance!
nutrient.adequate: Fertilizer should be applied at a maintenance rate to sustain current nutrient levels without causing accumulation.
nutrient.excess: Reduce or temporarily withhold fertilizer application to prevent nutrient buildup, leaching, and potential environmental impact!

disease.healthy: The majority of vegetation is healthy.
disease.low: Perform routine monitoring and take preventive action!
disease.severe: High severity level, immediate action required!
